elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted text says only "Contractor shall indemnify Company"; there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") obligation and no reference to Company's affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The indemnity runs to "Company" alone; affiliates are not named as indemnified parties.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: "any third-party claim alleging that the Services or the Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — Works are the contract's deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The inserted indemnity is limited to IP infringement/misappropriation claims; no breach-of-law trigger appears anywhere in Section 7 or elsewhere.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised-access/disclosure-of-Company-data trigger is included in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct trigger in the inserted indemnity; Section 7(a)/(b) caps and waivers remain without such a carve-out.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The insertion contains no notice mechanic.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No allocation of defence control (Contractor's option relates only to the procure/modify/replace remedies).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears in the inserted language.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the Agreement contains no Company indemnity of Contractor (Section 7 has only caps and waivers), and the redline does not introduce one, so nothing broader than the permitted scope exists.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall indemnify Company against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or the Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Exclusion (i) "modification of the Works by Company" — a permitted customary exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Exclusion (ii) "combination of the Works by Company with items not supplied by Contractor".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Exclusion (iii) "Contractor's compliance with specifications furnished by Company".

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall, at its option, procure for Company the right to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available, refund the fees paid to Contractor for the affected item".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "Notwithstanding Section 7(a), Contractor's liability under this Section 7(d) shall not exceed three times (3x) the annual fees paid to Contractor under this Agreement." The notwithstanding is necessary to displace the existing fees-paid cap, so the super-cap is operative rather than internally inconsistent.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all seven fallback elements appear in operative language (IP indemnity, the three customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace, refund, and a 3x annual fees super-cap expressly overriding the Section 7(a) fee cap).

Preferred is not met: the insertion lacks an express duty to defend, omits Company affiliates, and omits the breach-of-law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers as well as the notice/control/cooperation procedure. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add "defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates", limbs (b)-(d) of the model language, and a short claims procedure.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise paragraph confined to the fallback checklist; no existing Customer-favourable language (including the Section 5(c) non-infringement warranty and the Section 7(b) consequential-damages waiver) is deleted, and no extras such as survival tails, attorneys'-fee entitlements or added damages categories are introduced. The "Notwithstanding Section 7(a)" override is required by the super-cap element, not surplus.
Intent preserved: the liability cap, damages waiver and attorneys'-fees waiver survive and are not contradicted, save for the deliberate and necessary carve-out for the indemnity super-cap.

Drafting fix (non-fatal but should be repaired): the inserted paragraph carries no subsection label yet self-refers as "this Section 7(d)" — number the paragraph "(d)" so the cross-reference is not dangling. Consider also conforming the Section 7 heading, which still reads "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" while the new subsection is an indemnity from Contractor to Company.

Optional improvement within the fallback: the refund is limited to "fees paid ... for the affected item", which is acceptable, but pairing the indemnity with an express defence obligation would materially improve protection if the counterparty will accept it.
